pick.counterargument: It is an expensive stock: 55.6× trailing earnings and a 3.4% free cash flow yield, so the growth is already in the price and one weak quarter would cost a lot. growth decelerated against the previous quarter, so the trend in the numbers is already turning.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below +53.0%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $72.56 on the decision date.
risks: The share count is from 2026-09-30, 50 days older than the price, so the market capitalisation carries that staleness.
The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-09-30, 50 days before the decision date.
One of the four quarters in the trailing year is the fourth quarter, which companies report only as part of the full year; it is derived as the annual figure less the first three quarters.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-11-19.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2026-02-10) plus 364 days

pick.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
pick.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

sources.fundamentals: SEC Financial Statement Data Sets (twelve quarters), point-in-time by accepted timestamp, topped up from companyfacts for companies that have filed since the newest data set

stories.title: How to Refactor Python Code With an AI Agent
stories.excerpt: Learn how to refactor Python code with AI safely: find code smells, check that tests pin the behavior, and let an agent apply one refactoring at a time.
stories.lead:
Say you have a Python project that works, and nobody is filing bug reports for it. However, every change, fix, or new feature takes longer than it should and requires working on multiple files. Also, you try to avoid touching certain files because small changes there break the whole project. That’s called technical debt, and you can pay it down when you refactor Python code with AI.

Refactoring improves the code’s structure without changing what it does. This way, the next change will cost less than it would have before refactoring.

stories.title: Zelensky says Crimean Bridge strikes 'fair response' as he meets UK's Streeting
stories.excerpt: Ukraine's president says Kyiv acted after 109 separate Russian aerial attacks on bridges in Ukraine.
stories.lead:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has justified Kyiv's repeated attacks a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, calling it a "fair response" to 109 separate Russian attacks on bridges in Ukraine.

In comments to the BBC in Kyiv, Zelensky said the intense attacks on Ukraine by Russia that have followed the strikes on the Crimean Bridge were only a "signal that Vladimir Putin does not want to stop. He wants a reason to escalate".

He also rejected the claim the Russian president made in China that the bridge - which links Russia to the peninsular it illegally annexed from Ukraine - was "exclusively civilian" in use.

stories.title: Anthropic says it will put humanity first. Will its IPO change that?
stories.excerpt: Critics say now that the AI giant is a public company, its commitment to put safety ahead of commercial success will be tested.
stories.lead:
As Anthropic executives and co-founders gathered to celebrate the artificial intelligence company's market debut at the Nasdaq stock exchange on Thursday, CEO Dario Amodei spoke about AI's potential benefits, and risks, to humanity.

"There is a gigantic difference between how AI will go if we pay little attention to safety versus how it will go if we are obsessed with safety," Amodei said before ringing the ceremonial opening bell. "And an obsession with safety and public benefit has been built into Anthropic's DNA from the start."

stories.title: Denmark accuses Russia of plotting to assassinate US-Ukrainian rapper
stories.excerpt: The Russian embassy in Denmark has denied the allegation, which has led to Russia's defence attaché being expelled.
stories.lead:
Denmark has accused Russian intelligence services of plotting to assassinate a Ukrainian-American near Copenhagen, saying they had "planned" and "initiated" the attempt.

Denmark's security and intelligence agency (PET) said it had stopped individuals who were intending to kill the person, named by Danish media as rapper Kyivstoner, at a concert in September. Two people were charged with attempted murder and assisting a foreign intelligence service, and pleaded not guilty.

Denmark's foreign minister said Russia's defence attaché will now be expelled.

stories.title: An effort to circumvent the Electoral College may be within reach. But hurdles remain
stories.excerpt: A national effort to ensure that only winners of the popular vote become president could reach a critical milestone soon.
stories.lead:

Next year, Democrats will fully control five states that could sign the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact, an agreement among states to award their presidential electoral votes to the winner of the nationwide popular vote, not the winner of their respective states.

stories.title: Sessions offer advice on rising energy costs

Nora Corkery, chief executive of Devon Communities Together, said: "Behind every statistic is a household making difficult choices: rationing the heating, putting off filling up a tank, or cutting back on journeys they can't really do without."

The charity said people could access confidential one-to-one support to find financial help, with a limited number of free winter warm packs available for those who attend.

Cheryl Cottle-Hunkin, from Devon County Council, said: "I'd urge anyone who is struggling, or worried about the winter ahead, to seek advice and find out what help may be available."

stories.title: S&P 500 sinks 3.7% and the Nasdaq composite goes negative for the year
stories.excerpt: AI stocks have hefty market values and have a much bigger impact on the market's direction. They were responsible for Wall Street's big gains this year and are now behind the big slide for the market.
stories.lead:
NEW YORK — A bruising sell-off in artificial intelligence stocks on Friday pulled the S&P 500 down 3.7%, dragging the index to its worst weekly loss in more than 18 months, and knocking the Nasdaq composite into the red for the year.

The benchmark index is now in what professional investors call a "correction," having fallen more than 10% from its Oct. 6 all-time high.

The last time the S&P 500 had a correction was March 2025, as the Trump administration's trade war rattled the market. Its weekly loss, marking its worst such decline since April 2025, as the trade war escalated, capped a seven-day losing streak, the longest such string of losses since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020.
